abstracts.value: Reaction-amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem is limited by the bilinear form of all reaction observables. At fixed kinematics, N complex amplitudes contain 2N real quantities, whereas complete measurements determine at most 2N-1 parameters. Uniqueness therefore depends on whether additional physical constraints, such as unitarity, supply the missing information. We examine the consequences for resonance identification, focusing on angular-momentum assignments. Building on published results showing how truncation redistributes pole-bearing contributions among effective partial waves, we examine exact and practical ambiguities associated with imposing coupled-channel unitarity. A 4 x 4 counterexample shows that different on-shell unitary amplitudes can produce identical measurable bilinears. Practical unitary descriptions can also yield different pole content while remaining compatible with experimental uncertainties. We update Hoehler's clustering using the thirteen four-star N* resonances in PDG 2026 and Bonn-Gatchina results published in 2025. Nearby poles with different partial-wave assignments occur both in the PDG compilation and within Bonn-Gatchina, so their proximity is not solely a consequence of PDG averaging. Some groupings persist, while others change appreciably. We discuss a conditional interpretation in which truncation redistributes a common pole-bearing contribution among effective partial waves, with additional reconstruction uncertainties potentially accounting for departures from coincident pole positions. These considerations allow, but do not establish, a common origin for cluster members. The necessity of separate states and the stability of their angular-momentum assignments remain questions for further investigation.

titles.title: Non-uniqueness of the amplitude reconstruction in the inverse scattering problem and a refinement of Hoehler's resonance clustering

abstracts.value: Advances in free-electron quantum optics are establishing free electrons as a versatile quantum resource. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drift provide elementary operations for shaping the longitudinal electron wavefunction, yet their full control capabilities remain unexplored. Here, we prove that a finite sequence of alternating monochromatic PINEM interactions and free drifts can approximate any prescribed inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the full ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy. We therefore call the protocol PINEMAD (PINEM And Drift). This framework encompasses state preparation, unitary gates, and isometric encoding. We further show numerically that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads, using experimentally accessible coupling strengths and tabletop-scale total drift lengths. These results establish electron energy sidebands as a programmable quantum resource.

titles.title: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control

abstracts.value: We apply the numerically accurate multiple Davydov Ansatz (multi-$\rm D_2$) method to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of an open molecular cavity system using an extended driven-dissipative Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model incorporating Kerr nonlinearity. Our results reveal that the synergy between Kerr nonlinearity and exciton-phonon coupling induces an anharmonic level structure, imposing a stringent energy penalty that isolates the one-excitation manifold. This establishes a robust single-excitation-dominated regime that dynamically manifests photon blockade, characterized by suppression of the pure two-photon state and isolation of the one-excitation manifold. While strong coherent driving induces power broadening that overcomes the nonlinear barrier and opens multiphoton channels, cavity dissipation counteracts this process by acting as a highly selective manifold filter. By preferentially depleting fragile multi-photon states while sheltering single excitations within dissipation-free dark states, the cavity mode decay rate actively cooperates with Kerr nonlinearity to restore and reinforce the photon blockade effect. These findings elucidate the intricate interplay among nonlinearity, driving, and dissipation, offering a theoretical blueprint for engineering robust single-photon sources in open molecular cavity platforms.

titles.title: Cooperative Suppression of Two-Particle Excitation by Kerr Nonlinearity and Cavity Loss ion a Driven Holstein-Tavis-Cumming System

abstracts.value: We study back-to-back dijet production in deep inelastic scattering (DIS) at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on the quark-background contributions. We compute the quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections through next-to-leading power in the correlation limit for longitudinally and transversely polarized photons. In the quark-gluon channel, we derive both the kinematic corrections to the hard parts accompanying the twist-two quark distribution and the genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators. In the quark-antiquark channel, the interference of the eikonal amplitude with the double $t$-channel quark-exchange amplitudes probes three-body correlators with a different transverse arrangement of the fields. We express the results in terms of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlators and provide the corresponding hard coefficients. Our analysis extends the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark TMDs beyond leading power in the correlation limit.

titles.title: Twist-three quark TMDs from back-to-back dijet production in next-to-eikonal DIS

abstracts.value: Coherent orientations of extragalactic radio sources have been reported on large angular scales, but their statistical significance and susceptibility to observational systematics remain debated. Searches based on very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) also leave the far southern sky comparatively sparsely sampled. We test for local alignments of kiloparsec-scale radio source structural axes in the Sydney University Molonglo Sky Survey (SUMSS), providing a complementary probe in the undersampled southern sky. We constructed a catalog of structural position angles for 4087 sources from 629 SUMSS mosaics. A convolutional neural network supplied initial angle estimates, which were corrected for image-to-sky coordinate distortion and visually vetted. We searched for local alignments using a coordinate-invariant parallel transport statistic on HEALPix tessellations, then refined candidate regions with a genetic algorithm. We calibrated the significance of the full search against mock skies that preserve the declination-dependent position angle distribution and undergo the same search procedure. Several regions show apparently strong local alignment, but none remains statistically significant after accounting for the look-elsewhere effect. The candidate signals are consistent with chance fluctuations in the full search. We find no statistically significant evidence for alignment of structural axes of radio sources in SUMSS images. The resulting southern sky position angle catalog provides a useful resource for future studies of radio source morphology and population properties.

titles.title: Structural axes of sources in the SUMSS survey and their alignments

abstracts.value: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the $[Fe_4S_4(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by $\approx 534$ mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension $d = 3 \times 10^{10}$, we reach $E = -327.235076$ Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-$D = 4000$ DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and $\sim 512-517$ mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the $d \to \infty$ limit via a Gaussian-in-log $d$ fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate $E_\infty = -327.244468$ Ha $\pm 1.05$ mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate ($E_{D\to\infty} = -327.244797$ Ha $\pm 0.46$ mHa), well within their combined $1σ$ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on $[Fe_2S_2(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.

titles.title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy

abstracts.value: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

abstracts.value: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.

abstracts.value: Magnetic field detection is of great significance in modern fields such as medical diagnostics, geological exploration, inertial navigation, and space physics. We have previously investigated the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate. Building on these results, here we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient detection by establishing a quantitative relationship between the condensate's rotational deflection angle and the magnetic-field gradient. In this work, we present the parameter dependence of this scheme and perform a systematic optimization. We introduce a Bayesian optimization algorithm to automatically and efficiently search for the optimal combination of key parameters, thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity of the magnetic field gradient measurement. The results show that the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. This work not only provides a new approach for magnetic field gradient measurement but also serves as a reference for machine learning-empowered quantum precision measurement.

titles.title: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates

abstracts.value: We study the modular properties of torus correlators in a generalised Gibbs ensemble (GGE) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory. For the free fermion with KdV charges, we compute the exact two-point function and derive its modular $S$-transformation as a formal power series in the chemical potential. The transformed correlator admits a factorised description: an effective charge deforms the ensemble, while a local dressing operator acts on the external fields. Both are determined by nested operator product expansions involving the deforming current. Motivated by this result, we conjecture an analogous transformation law for $n$-point functions in rational chiral conformal field theories. Using Zhu's recursion, we establish the conjecture at the lowest explicit power of the modular parameter to all orders in the chemical potential, thereby determining the dressing operator. We also verify the full conjectured transformation through cubic order in the chemical potential, retaining all explicit powers of the modular parameter. These results extend the nested-OPE description of modular transformations of GGE partition functions to local correlation functions.

titles.title: Modular properties of correlators in generalised Gibbs ensembles

abstracts.value: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have attracted considerable attention for micro- and nanoscale thermometry owing to their high precision and spatial resolution. However, achieving sufficient electron spin polarization and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) typically requires high-power or long-duration laser excitation, which introduces heating and degrades measurement accuracy and stability. To address this trade-off, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach is proposed to optimize spin polarization under low-heating constraints. First, a physical model integrating five-level optical pumping rates and NV spin polarization dynamics is established. A temperature-rise constraint model is then developed based on pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (P-ODMR) measurements under varying laser powers and pulse widths in an external magnetic field. Subsequently, a Progressive Action-Space Q-learning (PAS-Q) algorithm is employed to explore the parameter space and identify optimal laser power and pulse-width combinations. The agent is trained through numerical simulations and the resulting strategy is implemented in a hardware system. Experimental results demonstrate a 44% reduction in laser-induced heating, a 33% increase in spin polarization rate based on T1 relaxation analysis, and a 71% reduction in optimization time compared with traditional methods. This approach enables efficient spin polarization with reduced laser heating and improved optimization efficiency, and may be extended to other heat-sensitive quantum spin sensors, including silicon-vacancy centers in diamond and divacancy defects in silicon carbide.

titles.title: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Based on PAS-Q

abstracts.value: ALICE experiment at the CERN's Large Hadron Collider, carried out a cosmic data-taking campaign in the period 2015-2018 (LHC Run 2), for a total of 62.5 days of real observation time. In this contribution, the analysis of these data is limited to multimuon events, i.e. events with more than four detected muons. In particular, the muon multiplicity distribution (MMD) is studied in the low-intermediate multiplicity range ($4 < N_μ < 50$), while for multiplicities $N_μ > 100$, dominated by large statistical fluctuations of the data, the rate of the high muon multiplicity events (HMM) is measured. The results are compared with Monte Carlo simulations using three of the main hadronic interaction models describing the air shower development in the atmosphere: QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC, and SIBYLL 2.3d, and assuming two extreme compositions of primary cosmic rays, pure proton and pure iron, representing respectively the lightest and the heaviest composition. Although the models have difficulty precisely describing the trend of primary p and Fe as a function of cosmic ray primary energy, QGSJET-II-04 is the only model that reproduces reasonably well the MMD and the rate of HMM events assuming a heavy composition for the entire energy range studied.

abstracts.value: Acorn tricks turn weak quantum resources into stronger "randomized" ones. A recent example is the random purification channel, which turns $t$ copies of a mixed state into $t$ copies of a random purification. We ask whether analogous techniques can turn queries to an isometry into queries to a random unitary completion, or queries to a quantum channel into queries to a random isometry dilation. For an isometry from dimension $N$ to dimension $M$, we give an efficient, stateful simulator for $T$ sequential, forward queries to a fixed Haar random unitary completion. It uses at most one forward isometry query per simulated call, with total trace-distance error $O(T\sqrt{N/(M-T)})$. This lifts isometry query lower bounds to arbitrary unitary completions, and copy complexity lower bounds to forward access to state preparation unitaries, with dimension-dependent loss that can be made arbitrarily small for most applications. Conversely, we construct two distributions on quantum channels distinguishable exactly with two queries to an arbitrary dilation, but requiring exponentially many channel queries for nonnegligible advantage. This rules out efficient simulation of random channel dilations. Our technique also shows that approximating the quantum switch to any constant error below $1/2$ requires exponentially many channel queries, even for identical channels, giving an exponential query advantage for indefinite causal order and improving on Bavaresco et al. (2025). Finally, we show how to "decontrol" controlled forward access to an isometry: any algorithm making controlled queries to $ϕV$ for a random phase $ϕ$ can be transformed into one using the same number of uncontrolled forward queries to $V$, generalizing the analogous result for unitaries.

titles.title: On Random Purifications of Isometries and Channels

abstracts.value: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. abstracts.value: Quantum simulations of molecular electronic structure hold the potential for computational advantage but are inherently limited by the linear scaling of qubit requirements with respect to system size. Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) addresses this constraint by reformulating the interacting many-body problem in terms of a non-interacting Kohn--Sham reference system. Here, we present and experimentally validate a Q-DFT algorithm that requires only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2(N))$ qubits to simulate a system of $N$ orbitals, thereby reducing resource overhead. More precisely, we solve the Kohn--Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using the ensemble extension of the variational quantum eigensolver paradigm that minimizes the energy of the system in the subspace spanned by the ground and first excited states. To execute this task, we encode the problem with qubits on a quantum photonic platform, utilizing an architecture that combines a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit. By evaluating the molecular ground- and first excited-state properties, this work establishes a pathway for simulating larger molecular systems, demonstrating the viability of integrating qubit-efficient algorithms with advanced reconfigurable photonic hardware for near-term quantum chemistry applications.

titles.title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit

abstracts.value: We study the entanglement dynamics of two qutrits under collective dephasing for a family of states obtained by mixing a maximally entangled state that lives in the decoherence-free subspace with three nonstationary two-term states sharing a common amplitude ratio $r$. We obtain exact PPT and separability regions along the whole trajectory, a specialization of known results on cyclic sign invariant states, and we supply explicit certificates: a finite product decomposition, three fixed positive-map witnesses, and a closed realignment formula that detects every PPT-entangled state, so that no state is left undecided. The negativity is computed in closed form. It shows that the entanglement is time-invariant, positive and constant from the initial time although the state changes, exactly when the weight of the maximally entangled state exceeds the threshold $U_r=r/(1+r+r^2)$. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of time-invariant entanglement for qutrit--qutrit systems under collective dephasing. For smaller weights the entanglement decays and vanishes at a finite time: the state either becomes separable (entanglement sudden death) or, for $r\neq1$ in an intermediate range, loses distillability suddenly and remains bound entangled at all later times. Every state with negative partial transpose is one-copy distillable by a fixed local projection. The same trajectories arise from the global dephasing map and from a correlated local random-unitary semigroup, although the two channels differ on product inputs. Exact rational benchmarks and embeddings of the Horodecki and Ha--Kye--Park families are provided.

titles.title: Time-invariant negativity and persistent bound entanglement in a cyclic two-qutrit family

abstracts.value: Mass inflation in non-extremal regular black holes with a non-linear dependence of the Misner-Sharp mass $M$ on the asymptotic mass $m>0$ may be a transient phenomenon followed by a model-dependent non-exponential late-time divergence. We analyse these regimes based on the generalised Ori model for a class of static spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat regular black holes with a de Sitter core and an $m$-independent upper bound on the Misner-Sharp mass density and Kretschmann scalar inspired by quasi-topological gravity. We discuss the geometric mechanism behind divergences of physical quantities at the inner horizon of the perturbed spacetime, and show that these require the unphysical mass parameter inside the shell to evolve outside the positive-real domain, or in some cases force a distinct type of dynamical continuation of the static metric. Imposing an asymptotic late-time divergence in form of a fractional power-law scaling, tunable to be arbitrarily mild within the considered approximation and effectively taming mass inflation, allows us to single out a family of generalised Fan-Wang regular black holes.

abstracts.value: Near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log T$ in the entropy. We ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order Lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic Lovelock term is dynamical. The multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. At fixed charge the Maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $S^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $K_J^{-1}$. As a result, the coefficient of $\log T$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive Gaussian value $19/2$. We compute the moment of inertia $K_J$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the Lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. Only large AdS black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. Adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. Its large-AdS limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound violation.

titles.title: Crossover from Schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal Lovelock black holes

abstracts.value: This article examines the instability of charged black holes, using Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory and a massless charged scalar field. Our study demonstrates that these black holes become unstable in a certain range of frequencies, which causes scalar "hair" to form outside the event horizon. By using numerical integration on the coupled field equations, we show that there is a phase transition between a purely charged black hole and a hairy black hole configuration. The results show that the hairy phase appears when the temperature is less than $T_C$, the critical temperature, whereas for $T>T_C$, the system stays purely charged. Also, our findings show that the critical temperature increases with the size of the black hole, implying that the onset of the phase transition becomes progressively more difficult for larger horizons. Lastly, we see that the system enters a stable equilibrium at the critical temperature, which is the final state of the superradiant instability. These results provide us with useful information on how nonlinear superradiant events change and how scalarized black holes arise in more comprehensive theories of gravity.

titles.title: Final state of superradiant instability in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black hole

abstracts.value: The astrophysical discovery potential of future gravitational wave detectors will hinge on accurate and rapid waveform generation. Third generation detectors are expected to observe many long duration compact binary coalescence signals that can probe binary formation and evolution as well as the nature of matter under extreme conditions. We develop a unified framework that combines physical modeling with deep learning. The framework uses an analytic residual spectral representation, shared learning, and decoders for each binary type. It generates waveforms for binary black holes, binary neutron stars, and neutron star black hole binaries, providing a single unified generator for all compact binary coalescences. The generated waveforms include the physical effects described by each reference model, such as spin precession, higher order modes, matter effects, and postmerger radiation for binary neutron stars. The waveforms span hundreds to thousands of cycles, with mean mismatches ranging from $5.89\times10^{-4}$ to $5.34\times10^{-2}$ relative to the reference waveforms. Batch generation achieves a maximum speedup of about 1800 over reference waveform generation.

abstracts.value: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

abstracts.value: Numerical simulation of field theories with complex actions is frustrated by the sign problem, which causes an exponential growth in statistical sampling noise. A key example of such a theory is QCD at finite baryon chemical potential, which has important applications to the structure of atomic nuclei and neutron stars. Until now, the sign problem has precluded the possibility of first-principles numerical calculations that could provide key insight into these important physical systems. In this work, we propose an approach to avoiding this limitation by applying a reweighting procedure coupled with a multi-level Monte-Carlo sampling algorithm that offers an exponential enhancement of statistics to counteract the sign problem. We test the approach on a simpler model that displays the same sign problem at finite chemical potential. Our results demonstrate the promise of the proposed approach, significantly increasing the range over which precise calculations are possible, and providing improvements all the way up to the phase transition.

titles.title: Can multi-level Monte-Carlo address the sign problem in a finite-density Bose gas?

abstracts.value: Exploring interactions between quantum emitters and guided photons, waveguide quantum electrodynamics (wQED) offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation and quantum interconnect. To simplify the quantized light-matter interactions, a linearized dispersion approximation (LDA) was widely used in wQED under the conditions of weak coupling and narrow photonic bandwidth. However, a growing number of strong-coupling wQED experiments have called the validity of LDA into question. Here, by investigating giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide, we propose a principle to judge the validity of LDA. We find that the decoherence of the atoms exhibits rich dynamical behaviors determined by different numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum (BICs and BOCs) formed in the energy spectrum of the total atom-photon system. Based on this, we show that despite the LDA can partially preserve some of BICs, it completely erases BOCs. This causes the dominant role of LDA in the atomic dynamics to break down. Providing a physical insight into the validity of LDA, our results lay a firm foundation for exploring fundamental physics and its application frontier in strong-coupling wQED platforms.

titles.title: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED

abstracts.value: Nuclear electric quadrupole moments of unstable isotopes are commonly extracted from laser spectroscopy of the atomic hyperfine structure, where the accuracy is limited to the several-percent level by the available electric-field-gradient (EFG) calculations. In this study, we determine the spectroscopic quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra (half-life $t_{1/2} = 11.4$ d) from hyperfine-resolved collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy of the radioactive molecule $^{223}$Ra$^{19}$F. The $X\,^2Σ^+$ electronic ground state of RaF provides a large axial EFG at the radium nucleus that can be calculated with relativistic coupled-cluster theory to sub-percent accuracy. Together with a three-fold improvement in spectral resolution over previous fast-beam measurements of radioactive molecules, this yields $Q_s = +1.211(7)_\mathrm{stat}(2)_\mathrm{syst}(5)_\mathrm{theo}\,e\mathrm{b}$ for $^{223}$Ra with a total uncertainty of 0.73%, approximately three times better than atomic and ionic determinations. This result demonstrates that molecular spectroscopy can provide access to the electromagnetic structure of unstable nuclei with a precision competitive with, and in favorable cases better than, atomic spectroscopy, and may thus be envisioned for studies beyond the limitations of current radioactive-atom experiments.

titles.title: Precise and accurate nuclear electric quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra from molecular spectroscopy

abstracts.value: Strongly correlated matter without quasiparticles is central to many-body physics, quantum chaos, and quantum gravity, motivating a considerable effort toward its realization in tabletop experiments. Two challenges remain: laboratory platforms are open systems, so conformal behavior must survive dissipation, and it must be identified through measurable quantities. We address both challenges in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, in which bosons and fermions interact as in, e.g., light-matter systems, but through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Solving the model in real time using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we treat closed and open systems within a unified framework and, in both cases, consider a thermal steady state to map their phase diagrams. In addition to the known conformal and impurity (or SYK$_2$) regimes, we identify novel high-temperature regimes in which the fermions are driven by an essentially bare boson and show that their dynamics is captured by a quadratic model with time-dependent random hopping. Across all regimes, the fermionic softening of the boson is bounded by a ``criticality budget'' determined only by the Yukawa coupling and the temperature. Coupling the boson with a thermal environment induces a mass shift that deforms the boundaries between different regimes and exhausts the criticality budget, thus imposing a bound on temperature and dissipation rate compatible with self-tuned criticality. We further introduce a set of markers built from the two-point functions that separate all identified regimes, are accessible in linear response, and require no fit of the conformal exponents. We complement them with the quantum Fisher information, deriving upper bounds with and without dissipation. These results may help characterize holographic quantum matter beyond the closed setting.

titles.title: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time

abstracts.value: Recent studies show that in addition to the flat spacetime, Integration-by-parts (IBP) relations and differential equations can also provide a systematic approach to Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime. dSIBP is a Mathematica package for the automated construction of IBP systems and differential equations. For dS integral families with massive and massless propagators, it generates a complete set of IBP seeds, assembles linear systems for external reduction, and constructs differential equations for the reduced master integrals. The implementation combines equations of motion, remaining terms and parity constraints, and provides reliable checks. We describe the conventions and public interface through worked examples.

abstracts.value: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

titles.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC

abstracts.value: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons. These results establish engineered system-bath coupling and nonlinear interactions as a route to suppress dissipation of chiral topological edge transport.

titles.title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators

abstracts.value: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.

titles.title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters

abstracts.value: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ ΛΛ\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(π\), \(η\), \(σ\), \(ρ\), \(ω\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(η\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

titles.title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+ΛΛ$ reaction

abstracts.value: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.

titles.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion

abstracts.value: We measure the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $π^+π^-/μ^+μ^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_μ^{ππ}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

titles.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar

abstracts.value: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to π^+π^-(γ)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$Υ(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $π^+π^-$ to $μ^+μ^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

titles.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar

Introduction
One of the central challenges in string theory is to determine whether it admits phe-nomenologically viable four-dimensional vacua. A realistic compactification should re-produce, at sufficiently low energies, the essential features of observed particle physics.A widely studied possibility is that the resulting four-dimensional theory contains an
N = 1 supersymmetric matter sector, with supersymmetry spontaneously broken atan energy scale compatible with phenomenological constraints. The properties of thefour-dimensional effective theory are determined by the vacuum configuration of thecompactification. In particular, quantities such as gauge couplings, Yukawa couplings,particle masses, and supersymmetry-breaking parameters depend on the vacuum ex-pectation values of scalar fields known as moduli. These fields parametrise continuousdeformations of the internal geometry, as well as other background data characterisingthe compactification.

For a long time, the presence of unstabilised moduli represented one of the mainobstacles to connecting string theory with low-energy phenomenology. Massless mod-uli would mediate long-range fifth forces and, since their vacuum expectation valuesenter directly into physical observables, would prevent the theory from making definitepredictions. Although perturbative and non-perturbative quantum effects are generi-cally expected to generate a potential for the moduli in four-dimensional N = 1 the-ories, a systematic and parametrically controlled mechanism for stabilising all of themremained unavailable for many years.

A major advance was provided by the development of flux compactifications and bythe systematic study of their role in moduli stabilisation [7–9]. Type IIB string compact-ifications provide a particularly suitable setting for this programme. In this framework,background three-form fluxes generate a superpotential for the axio-dilaton S and thecomplex-structure moduli za, allowing these fields to be stabilised at tree level. TheKähler moduli Tα, by contrast, remain unfixed at this order as a consequence of the no-scale structure of the tree-level effective theory. Their stabilisation therefore requireseffects that are absent at the classical level. In particular, the interplay between non-perturbative contributions to the superpotential [10] and perturbativeα′ corrections tothe Kähler potential [11,12] generates a non-trivial scalar potential for the Kähler sector.This potential can be analysed within a controlled expansion at large internal volumeand leads to the Large Volume Scenario [1], in which the overall volume of the compact-ification is stabilised at an exponentially large value. Such vacua provide a particularlyrich framework for studying supersymmetry breaking and its possible phenomenologi-
1



cal consequences.

The resulting hierarchy naturally suggests a two-step treatment of moduli stabili-sation. One first determines the supersymmetric tree-level vacuum of the axio-dilatonand complex-structure sector by imposing the supersymmetric condition, and subse-quently, treats the fields (S, za) as effectively frozen while analysing the subleadingdynamics responsible for the stabilisation of the Kähler moduli. This procedure cap-tures the leading structure of the vacuum and forms the basis of the conventional four-dimensional LVS effective theory. However, the separation between the two sectors isnot exact. The perturbative and non-perturbative effects responsible for Kähler-modulistabilisation depend, in general, on the axio-dilaton and complex-structure moduli. Oncethese contributions are included, the complete scalar potential develops non-vanishinggradients along the (S, za) directions. Consequently, the original tree-level flux vac-uum is displaced from its supersymmetric position [2,6]. The assumption that the flux-stabilised fields remain exactly frozen therefore neglects their backreaction on the fullvacuum.

The purpose of this thesis is to investigate this effect systematically. In particular, wedetermine explicitly the displacement of the axio-dilaton and complex-structure vac-uum induced by the subleading corrections responsible for Kähler-moduli stabilisation.The corrected minimum is computed perturbatively around the tree-level flux vacuum,organising the analysis according to the parametric dependence on the compactifica-tion volume V and the string coupling gs. Our results are derived in the controlledregime of exponentially large volume and weak string coupling,
V ≫ 1, gs ≪ 1. (0.1)

This allows us to identify the leading contributions to the vacuum shifts and to de-termine their scaling in the simultaneous large-volume and weak-coupling expansions.Once the corrected vacuum configuration has been determined, one can compute thecorrespondingF -terms, which provide the relevant order parameters for supersymme-try breaking in the four-dimensional effective theory.

A central result of this analysis is that the contribution induced by the displacementof the vacuum is not parametrically negligible. For the axio-dilaton, the shift-inducedcorrection enters at the same order in the simultaneous expansions in gs and V−1 asthe contribution obtained by evaluating the corrected F -terms at the unshifted tree-level vacuum. In the complex-structure direction, the effect is even more pronounced:
2



the shift-induced contribution is enhanced by an additional factor of g−1
s relative tothe corresponding unshifted term. Therefore, despite the smallness of the vacuum dis-placement itself, its effect on the F -terms can be of leading-order relevance, in theweak-coupling regime.We first study this mechanism in a simplified model with a rigid complex-structuresector, in which only the axio-dilaton S is displaced. We then extend the analysis toa model containing a dynamical complex-structure modulus and explicitly account forthe mixing between the S and z directions. This allows us to determine both the para-metric behaviour and the explicit form of the shifts δS and δz in the large-volume andweak-coupling expansions.

As previously stated, the corrections to the axio-dilaton and complex-structure F -terms can have direct phenomenological consequences. In sequestered LVS scenarios,soft supersymmetry-breaking terms depend sensitively on the auxiliary fields of theflux-stabilized sector [3]. We find that the shift of the vacuum does not parametricallymodify F S , so that soft terms whose leading contribution is controlled by the axio-dilaton auxiliary field retain the standard LVS scaling. By contrast, the modified complex-structure F -terms can give parametrically different contributions to observables whichdepend directly on F z, including scalar masses in the ultra-local regime.A further application concerns the supersymmetric partners of closed-string hiddenphotons. In type IIB orientifold compactifications, RR photons arise from the dimen-sional reduction of the RR four-form C(4) on orientifold-even three-cycles, and theirgauge kinetic functions are controlled by the complex-structure moduli [4, 13]. Con-sequently, the corresponding hidden-photino masses depend directly on the complex-structure F -terms. Therefore, any parametric modification of F za induced by the dis-placement of the flux vacuum is directly inherited by the hidden-photino mass, up tothe model-dependent complex-structure dependence of the gauge kinetic function.These examples provide a direct connection between the corrections studied in thiswork and the low-energy phenomenology of sequestered string compactifications.

This thesis is organised as follows. The first two chapters provide the theoreticalbackground required for the subsequent analysis. After reviewing the essential ele-ments of four-dimensional supergravity, we introduce the main features of superstringtheory and of Type IIB compactifications. Particular attention is devoted to the fieldcontent and effective description of Type IIB orientifolds with O3/O7-planes, with theaim of defining the quantities and conventions needed throughout the rest of the the-sis. Chapter 3 is devoted to the problem of moduli stabilisation. We first discuss the roleof background fluxes in fixing the axio-dilaton and complex-structure moduli and thenintroduce the Large Volume Scenario as a mechanism for stabilising the Kähler sector.

3



In this context, we emphasise the conventional two-step procedure in which the fluxsector is stabilised at tree level and subsequently treated as effectively frozen whenanalysing the subleading Kähler-moduli dynamics. The final chapter contains the orig-inal results of this work. We compute explicitly the displacement of the flux-stabilisedvacuum induced by the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections responsible forLVS stabilisation. The analysis is first carried out in a simplified toy model with rigidcomplex structure and is then extended to a more general setting including a dynamicalcomplex-structure modulus. We finally determine the corresponding corrections to theaxio-dilaton and complex-structure F -terms and analyse their parametric behaviour inthe large-volume and weak-coupling regime.

4



1 Supersymmetry and Supergravity
Supersymmetry is a spacetime symmetry relating bosonic and fermionic degrees offreedom and organizing them into common supermultiplets. It plays a fundamentalrole in superstring theory, whose development was historically motivated by the at-tempt to incorporate fermionic excitations into the bosonic string.The low-energy dynamics of string compactifications is naturally described in termsof supersymmetric field theories. In four-dimensional compactifications preserving foursupercharges, the relevant framework is N = 1 supersymmetry. We therefore beginthis chapter by reviewing the basic structure of four-dimensional rigid supersymmetry,introducing its algebra, the corresponding supermultiplets, and the supersymmetric ac-tions.We then turn to local supersymmetry, obtained by promoting the parameters of su-persymmetry transformations to spacetime-dependent spinors. Such a local symmetrycannot be consistently realized without introducing gravity: the corresponding gaugetheory necessarily contains the graviton, together with its fermionic superpartner, thegravitino. The resulting framework is N = 1, D = 4 supergravity.Finally, we present the supergravity action for chiral and vector multiplets coupledto gravity, emphasizing the role of the Kähler potential, the superpotential, and thegauge kinetic functions. Particular attention will be devoted to the scalar potential andto the auxiliary F -terms, which provide the essential language for describing modulistabilization and supersymmetry breaking in four-dimensional effective theories arisingfrom string compactifications.

1.4 Supersymmetry breaking
If supersymmetry is realized in Nature, it cannot be an exact symmetry at the energyscales currently accessible to experiments. Indeed, exact supersymmetry would requirethe bosonic and fermionic states belonging to the same supermultiplet to have identicalmasses. No such mass degeneracy has been observed in the spectrum of elementaryparticles.Supersymmetry must therefore be broken at some characteristic scale, which wedenote by MSUSY. At energies much larger than this scale, the effects responsiblefor the breaking may become negligible, and the theory approaches its supersymmet-ric limit. This statement is particularly natural when supersymmetry is broken by softterms.There are two conceptually distinct ways in which supersymmetry may be broken:

• Spontaneous supersymmetry breaking. The Lagrangian is exactly supersymmet-ric, but the vacuum is not invariant under the action of the supercharges. In aglobally supersymmetric theory, this occurs when at least one auxiliary field ac-quires a non-vanishing vacuum expectation value.
• Explicit supersymmetry breaking. The Lagrangian contains terms which are not in-variant under supersymmetry transformations. A generic explicit breaking wouldspoil the ultraviolet cancellations which motivate supersymmetry. One thereforeusually restricts to soft supersymmetry-breaking terms, which do not reintroducequadratic ultraviolet divergences. Their coefficients have positive mass dimen-sion, so their effects become progressively less important at energies much largerthan the supersymmetry-breaking scale.
Typical soft-breaking operators include scalar mass terms, gaugino masses and scalartrilinear and bilinear interactions. Although these terms explicitly break supersymme-try, they preserve the improved ultraviolet behaviour of the supersymmetric theory.

2 Superstrings
In this chapter, we review the main ingredients of type II superstring theory that arerequired for the compactification framework developed in the remainder of this thesis[15]. We begin with the Ramond–Neveu–Schwarz formulation of superstrings in ten-dimensional flat Minkowski spacetime, emphasizing the role of worldsheet fermions,the Neveu–Schwarz and Ramond sectors, and the GSO projection. The latter removesthe tachyonic state and leads to a spectrum containing both spacetime bosons andfermions, organized into supersymmetric multiplets.Among the five consistent superstring theories in ten dimensions, type IIA, type IIB,type I, and the two heterotic theories with gauge groups SO(32) and E8 × E8, wefocus on the type II theories, and in particular on type IIB string theory, which providesthe ten-dimensional starting point for the compactifications considered in this work.We therefore review it massless spectra and its corresponding low-energy supergravitydescriptions.We then turn to compactifications on Calabi–Yau threefolds. After introducing thegeometric and cohomological properties of Calabi–Yau manifolds, we discuss how theten-dimensional massless fields give rise to four-dimensional fields through Kaluza–Klein reduction. Compactification of type II string theory on a Calabi–Yau threefold pre-servesN = 2 supersymmetry in four dimensions. To obtain theN = 1 effective theoryrelevant for moduli stabilization, we subsequently introduce orientifold projections andspecialize to type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifolds withO3/O7-planes. This construction de-termines the surviving moduli fields and their organization into four-dimensional chiraland vector multiplets, providing the setting in which fluxes, the effective Kähler poten-tial, and the corrections to the moduli F -terms will be studied.

By contrast, type IIA supergravity is non-chiral: its fermionic degrees of freedom occur with opposite chiralities, and the theoryis therefore free of local perturbative gravitational anomalies.In the following, we restrict attention to the bosonic two-derivative actions in stringframe. 2.3 Type II Compactifications
We now discuss how the ten-dimensional supergravity theories arising as the low-energylimits of type II string theories can be reduced to four dimensions. In the simplest classof compactifications, one considers an unwarped product geometry of the form

M10 =M4 ×X6, (2.47)
where M4 is a four-dimensional spacetime and X6 is a compact six-dimensional inter-nal manifold. At this stage, we assume that the dilaton is constant and that all back-ground form-field strengths vanish, so that the only non-trivial background field is theten-dimensional metric.If the compactification is required to preserve part of the ten-dimensional super-symmetry, the geometry of X6 is strongly constrained. Compactification of either typeIIA or type IIB supergravity on a Calabi–Yau threefold with holonomy exactlySU(3) pre-serves eight real supercharges and therefore gives an N = 2 supersymmetric theoryin four dimensions. Additional ingredients, such as orientifold projections, are requiredto reduce the supersymmetry further to N = 1.

Let us first explain why Calabi–Yau manifolds naturally arise in supersymmetry-preservingcompactifications. In a purely geometric background, with vanishing fluxes and con-stant dilaton, the supersymmetry variation of the gravitino requires the ten-dimensionalsupersymmetry parameter ϵ to be covariantly constant,

2.4 Type II orientifolds
Orientifold projections of Type II Calabi–Yau compactifications provide a standard mech-anism for reducing four-dimensional supersymmetry from N = 2 to N = 1. They in-troduce orientifold planes and require the inclusion of D-branes for Ramond–Ramondcharge cancellation, thereby also giving rise to gauge sectors and charged matter in thefour-dimensional effective theory.Starting from Type II string theory compactified on a Calabi–Yau threefold X3, onequotients the theory by a discrete orientifold action involving worldsheet parity and aninvolution of the internal manifold. Depending on the Type II theory and on the classof orientifold, the orientifold operator takes the form

O = (−1)FLΩσ. (2.83)
Here Ω reverses the orientation of the string worldsheet, FL is the spacetime fermionnumber in the left-moving sector, and σ is an involutive isometry of the internal Calabi–Yau manifold,

σ2 = id. (2.84)
The precise form of O, as well as the action of σ on the Calabi–Yau geometry, dependson the orientifold construction under consideration.The geometric fixed loci of σ support orientifold planes. An Op-plane extends alongthe four non-compact spacetime dimensions and wraps an internal cycle of real dimen-sion p−3. In the standard orientifold constructions considered here, these objects carrynegative Ramond–Ramond charge and negative tension. Their total Ramond–Ramondcharge must be cancelled by appropriate configurations of D-branes and, when rele-vant, background fluxes. This requirement is encoded in the corresponding Ramond–Ramond tadpole-cancellation conditions.Spacetime-filling D-branes extend along the four non-compact dimensions and wrapinternal cycles of X3. They need not wrap the same cycles as the orientifold planes.Rather, the total charge carried by the D-branes and their orientifold images must can-cel the charges of the orientifold planes, together with any flux-induced contributions,in the appropriate homology or cohomology class. Open strings ending on the D-branesgive rise to four-dimensional gauge fields and charged matter multiplets.Preservation of four-dimensional N = 1 supersymmetry imposes further condi-tions on the involution σ. In Type IIB orientifolds, σ acts holomorphically on the Calabi–Yau manifold, whereas in the standard Type IIA constructions it acts antiholomorphi-cally. Its action assigns definite parities to the Kähler form J , the holomorphic three-form Ω, and the ten-dimensional form fields. The orientifold projection retains onlythe degrees of freedom invariant under the combined action O, thereby truncating theoriginal four-dimensional N = 2 spectrum to an N = 1 spectrum.

3 Large Volume Scenario
The four-dimensional massless spectrum arising from string compactifications gener-ally contains a large number of scalar fields, known as moduli. In Type IIB Calabi–Yauorientifold compactifications with O3/O7-planes, whose field content is summarized inTable 2, these fields parametrise continuous deformations of the internal geometry anddetermine several effective four-dimensional couplings. If they remain unstabilized, themoduli correspond to flat directions of the scalar potential and may give rise to lightscalar degrees of freedom. Such fields can mediate long-range interactions and inducephenomenological effects that are incompatible with current observations. A realisticstring compactification must therefore provide a mechanism that lifts these flat direc-tions, fixes the vacuum expectation values of the moduli, and generates sufficientlylarge masses for them.In this chapter, we review the Large Volume Scenario (LVS), which provides a sys-tematic framework for moduli stabilization in Type IIB flux compactifications. The sta-bilization mechanism proceeds hierarchically. At leading order, background three-formfluxes stabilize the axio-dilaton and the complex-structure moduli at a supersymmetricminimum, while the Kähler moduli remain unfixed as a consequence of the no-scalestructure. Their stabilization is subsequently achieved by including perturbative α′ cor-rections to the Kähler potential together with non-perturbative contributions to the su-perpotential. This two-step structure will play a central role in the analysis developedin the remainder of this thesis.

5 Conclusions and Outlook
The Large Volume Scenario is commonly analysed through a two-step procedure. Attree level, background fluxes stabilise the axio-dilaton and the complex-structure mod-uli at a supersymmetric vacuum, while the Kähler moduli remain unfixed because ofthe no-scale structure. Perturbative and non-perturbative effects are then included tostabilise the Kähler sector, treating the flux-stabilised fields as effectively frozen at theirtree-level values.This separation provides a controlled description of the vacuum at leading orderin the inverse-volume expansion. It is, however, not exact. The effects responsible forKähler-moduli stabilisation depend in general on the axio-dilaton and complex-structuremoduli and therefore generate non-vanishing gradients along these directions. As aconsequence, the tree-level flux vacuum is displaced once the complete scalar poten-tial is taken into account.The purpose of this thesis has been to study this displacement systematically andto determine how it modifies the auxiliary fields associated with the flux-stabilised sec-tor. Particular attention has been devoted to the simultaneous large-volume and weak-coupling expansions,

V ≫ 1, gs ≪ 1, (5.1)
which provide the parametric control required by the four-dimensional effective de-scription.The corrected vacuum was determined perturbatively by separating the scalar po-tential into its leading flux contribution and the subleading terms. This procedure makesexplicit that the magnitude of the displacement is determined not only by the correct-ing potential, but also by the inverse Hessian of the tree-level flux vacuum. The lattercarries a non-trivial dependence on the string coupling and plays an essential role inthe final power counting.In the first simplified model, the only displaced flux-stabilised field is the axio-dilaton.The calculation showed that the shift of S generates an additional contribution to itsauxiliary field F S . This contribution scales parametrically as

Nevertheless, itcontributes to the numerical coefficient ofF S at the first non-vanishing order and mustconsequently be included in a complete computation at this accuracy.

Analysis of the harmonic flow

of geometric structures

Eric Loubeau
Département de Mathématiques
LMBA / UMR 6205
Université de Bretagne Occidentale
6, avenue Victor Le Gorgeu
CS 93837, 29238 Brest Cedex 3, France
eric.loubeau@univ-brest.fr

Received: March 5, 2025; accepted: June 10, 2025.

Abstract. We develop an analysis of the flow of harmonic H-structures with the strategy
introduced by Chen-Struwe for the harmonic map heat equation when the target does not
necessarily have negative sectional curvature, so the Eells-Sampson Theorem cannot apply.

In particular, this flow method enables us to find theoretical hypotheses under which the
existence of a torsion-free H-structure is guaranteed and conditions for which the flow must
blow up in finite time.

This extends results already known for some specific groups like U(n), G2 or Spin(7).

Keywords: Geometric structures; harmonic maps; harmonic sections, heat flow

MSC 2020 classification: primary 53C10, 53C15, 53C43, 58E20, 53E30

1 Holonomy and geometric structures

Berger’s 1955 theorem gives the list of the seven possible holonomy groups
of an irreducible, non-symmetric, simply-connected Riemannian n-dimensional
manifold: SO(n) (the general case), U(n2 ) (Kähler), SU(n2 ) (Calabi-Yau), Sp(n4 )
(Hyper-Kähler), Sp(n4 )Sp(1) (Quaternionic-Kähler), G2 (n = 7), Spin(7) (n =
8); plus the group Spin(9) for n = 16, before it was removed by Alekseevskij [1].

Moreover, each case is characterised by the existence of a parallel (multi-)
tensor, with respect to the Levi-Civita connection of (M, g).

For SO(n), it is the unobstructed condition of a torsion-free connection,
the Kähler case is equivalent to the existence of a parallel almost Hermitian
structure, etc.

For G2, the parallel three-form ϕ must, point-wise, be given in some frame
of TpM by

ϕp = e123 − e1 ∧ (e45 − e67) + e2 ∧ (e46 − e57) + e3 ∧ (e47 − e56),

http://siba-ese.unisalento.it/ © 2025 Università del Salento



130 E. Loubeau

while for Spin(7), Φ ∈ Λ4(T ∗M) and the local model is

Φp = e0123 − e0145 − e0167 − e0246 + e0257 − e0347 − e0356

+ e4567 − e2367 − e2345 − e1357 + e1346 − e1256 − e1247

where

e0123 = dx0 ∧ dx1 ∧ dx2 ∧ dx3.

The significance of holonomy is twofold. First, it informs on the curvature tensor
as it must live in the holonomy Lie algebra and this implies for SU(n2 ), Sp(n4 ),
G2 and Spin(7) that the manifold is Ricci-flat.

On the other hand, manifolds with special holonomy are the cornerstone
of higher-dimensional Gauge Theory. For example, take n = 7 and G2, then
a vector bundle E → M7 with connection ∇ has curvature F∇ ∈ Λ2, so the
condition ∗F∇ = λF∇ (λ ∈ R) does not make sense anymore and we must
introduce a three-form to counterbalance the degrees. If chosen closed, it will
allow for Yang-Mills connections.

The disadvantage is that it is generally hard to construct manifolds with spe-
cial holonomy, as the problem is highly non-linear, especially when the defining
tensor determines the metric. For example, local solutions of G2-manifolds first
appear in 1984 [3], complete ones in 1986 [4] and compact constructions only as
late as 1996-2000 with Joyce [15, 16].

An alternative, softer and more topological in nature, is to consider H-
structures (H ⊂ SO(n)), which are reductions of the structure group and can
also be seen as sections of an ad-hoc twistor space constructed as the H-quotient
of the unitary frame bundle PSO(n).

Locally, H-structures are described by (multi-) tensors given at each point
by a Euclidean prototype and stabilized by the group H.

It relies on a model (p, q)-tensor ξ0 ∈ T p,q(Rn) on the Euclidean space,
stabilised by the group H = Stab(ξ0) = {g ∈ GL(n,R) : g.ξ0 = ξ0} under the
GL(n,R) right action

g.ξ0 = ξ

The energy functional is conformally invariant when dimM = 2 and harmonic

The groundbreaking work of Eells and Sampson [10] did not just introduced
this notion but also proved the existence of a harmonic representative in each
homotopy class when the target has non-positive sectional curvature. One should
however keep in mind that if there only exists a single homotopy class, it will
contain the trivially-harmonic constant maps.

Perhaps, as important was the heat-flow method they employed which has
known a rich legacy, all the way to Hamilton’s Ricci flow and Perelman’s proof
of the Poincaré conjecture.

This method is perhaps just as compelling by its failure when the curvature
condition on the target is not met and the flow develops bubbles and explodes,
as is the case of the sphere S2 to itself. This was superbly exploited by Sachs
and Uhlenbeck with a reparametrization process enabling to restart the flow
and accounting for the topological penalties in terms of energy quantization.

Paradoxically, for the two-sphere, these pitfalls of the heat flow can eas-
ily be circumvented by considering holomorphic maps and produce harmonic
representatives in each and every homotopy class.

The best-known situation where harmonic maps do not exist is for degree-
one maps from the two-torus to the two-sphere [11]. Indeed, such a map would

Riemann-Roch.

In higher dimensions, one of the most often encountered example is the Hopf
map from S3 to S2 and, as a Riemannian submersion with minimal fibres, it also
happens to be a harmonic morphism.

In spite of decades of work on harmonic maps, relatively little has been done
for sections, except perhaps for vector fields [7], and C. M. Wood was the first to
consider almost Hermitian structures as sections of the twistor space and study
them under the light of harmonicity [20].

The point here is not merely to compute the tension field of a particular
map but more precisely to consider the Dirichlet energy of sections and search
for its critical points among sections, in order to compare like with like.

On a philosophical level, there is no reason to limit this to the specific case
of almost Hermitian structures and any type of reduction of structures on a
Riemannian manifold can be the subjected to the same treatment.

3 The Heat flow

The ultimate objective of the heat flow of geometric structures is to pro-
vide conditions ensuring the existence of an absolute minimiser of the Dirichlet
energy and answer the question of torsion-free geometric structures in a given
homotopy class.

With a target of positive curvature, one cannot hope to apply Eells-Sampson’s
original proof and must turn to Chen-Struwe’s arguments. In the end, this ap-
proach leads to a threshold for the Dirichlet energy of the initial data under
which convergence will happen to a torsion-free solution. By contraposition,
this lower bound can also be used to obtain singularity results.

This method is based on a series of more or less technical results but first,
one should recall that short-time existence is an automatic consequence of the
harmonic map equation. The main equation we will work with is the Bochner
formula which essentially turns the heat flow equation, living in the pull-back
of the vertical space of the twistor space, i.e. the bundle associated with the
isotropic representation, into a scalar expression at the cost of becoming an
inequality.

The Shi-type estimates control, along the flow, the norms of the derivatives
of the torsion (basically the coderivatives of the geometric structure) in terms
of the torsion itself and the derivatives of the curvature.

Both these results are valid for a general group H ⊂ SO(n) (and even more
cf. [9]).

The cornerstone of the whole strategy is the Almost Monotonicity Formula
(AMF) for a time-dependent functional which integrates, over a geodesic ball,
the product of the energy density and the backward heat kernel with singularity
at the centre of the ball (along with localisation by a cut-off function).



138 E. Loubeau

This AMF will prompt the ε-regularity of the heat flow which draws a point-
wise bound of the energy density from a bound on the integral of the function
involved in the AMF.

This opens the gates, not only for energy gap results but also for long-time
existence and finite-time singularity statements.

Indeed, by a refined treatment of the Bochner formula, due to Chen-Ding
[5], controlling the existence interval of the harmonic flow, one can prove that
if the energy density remains bounded over the maximal existence interval then
the flow exists for all time and converges to a harmonic solution.

On the other hand, if it explodes then the maximal existence-time must be
less than (the square-root of) the initial energy.

To conclude, bounds on the Dirichlet energy and L∞-norm of the initial data
exclude explosion of the energy density over the maximal existence interval,
hence force long-time existence and convergence toward a torsion-free solution.

Additionally, if no torsion-free H-structure exists in a given homotopy class
while the infimum of the Dirichlet energy is indeed zero, small enough initial
Dirichlet energy will make the flow develop a finite-time singularity.

Versions of these results for specific groups H can be found in [14, 8] but
note that groups like SU(n) are not covered by these results.

abstracts.value: Recently, influence of strong fields on nuclear decay processes is progressively becoming a topic of great interest plus the existence of some ambiguities. In this study, an approximate calculation of the Schrödinger equation with reduced <math><mi>r</mi></math> dependence is employed instead of the classical Coulomb wave-function program to provide a description of decay width and decay energy in quasistatic (adiabatic) laser fields. More importantly, going beyond the quasistatic approximation, the strict time evolution of the wave function and the periodic modulation of the decay energy are investigated by solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation with the split operator method, which captures the dynamical behavior of the <math><mi>α</mi></math> cluster during the decay process. First, our results corroborate earlier reports that the decay width is modified only negligibly by strong laser fields. Likewise, the shift in decay energy is found to be extremely small, which validates the rationality of using fixed experimental decay energies in earlier studies. This modification effect will exist more obviously in a nucleus with the higher proton-neutron asymmetry, the lower decay energy, and the octupole deformation. Second, our results demonstrate that strong fields can indeed produce a periodic modulation of decay energy, with a cycle mean shift on the order of <math><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>eV</mi></mrow></math> at an intensity of <math><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>24</mn></msup><mspace width="4pt"/><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>.

titles.title: Time evolution of the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay process in intense laser fields

abstracts.value: Spin squeezing is a genuine multipartite entanglement resource enabling quantum-enhanced metrology beyond classical limits. Based on a hybrid solid-state system of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and magnons, we propose a scheme for generating spin squeezing via Kerr nonlinearity. In the large-detuning regime, by tuning the strength of the magnon parametric amplification (MPA) enabled by Kerr effect, the magnon-mediated spin-spin interactions can be controlled, thereby allowing flexible switching among one-axis twisting (OAT), two-axis twisting (TAT), and unconventional two-axis twisting (UTAT). Remarkably, in the presence of realistic dissipation and finite-size effects, an optimized UTAT interaction exhibits enhanced spin squeezing and quantum-enhanced sensing performance compared with the corresponding OAT and TAT cases. Furthermore, in the resonant and strongly dissipative regime, the MPA-induced TAT interaction and squeezed magnon reservoir jointly enable steady-state spin squeezing of the NV ensemble. Our results establish a unified and flexible scheme for generating both dynamical and steady-state spin squeezing, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced precision measurements.

titles.title: Dynamical and stable spin squeezing via magnon Kerr nonlinearity in a hybrid solid-state system

abstracts.value: We design an atom-waveguide system to achieve nonreciprocal frequency conversion. Single-photon frequency conversion is achieved through inelastic scattering mediated by the V-type giant atom with one transition coupled to a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide (CRW) and the other transition coherently driven by a classical field. To quantitatively characterize the frequency-conversion efficiency, we define scattering flows by incorporating the corresponding group velocities. The reciprocity and nonreciprocity of the system can be characterized by the conversion-flow contrast. It is found that the single-photon frequency-conversion flow is closely related to the size of the giant atom and the phase difference between the coupling strengths at the two atom-CRW coupling sites. Under reciprocal conditions, the maximum conversion flow is strictly bounded by <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, regardless of how the giant atom size and the phase difference are tuned. When reciprocity is broken, tuning the coupling phase at a fixed giant atom size significantly enhances the maximum conversion flow, which can even reach unity. Meanwhile, the conversion-flow contrast reaches its extremal values, corresponding to perfect single-photon nonreciprocity.

titles.title: Nonreciprocal frequency conversion of single photons in a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide
